title: Mark generated formatters and resolvers as excluded from code coverage

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).
All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.

requirement.title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement.intent: Code generated by MessagePack must be excluded from code coverage reports by the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

functional.text: All generated code is decorated with the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.
No setting is needed to turn the attribute on.
The attribute is added whichever kind of type is generated (formatters, enum formatters, resolvers).
A GeneratedCode attribute on the generated types is optional.

nonFunctional.text: The attribute must not break builds for target frameworks that lack it. (inferred)
Existing generated output stays the same apart from the attribute. (inferred)

derivedFrom.note: Derived by the engine lane from the upstream issue text on 2026-11-14; not Tieto's requirements set.

expectedBehaviours: Every type the source generator emits carries the System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.
Coverage tools such as coverlet leave generated formatter and resolver code out of their reports.
The generator snapshot outputs under Resources show the attribute on each generated type declaration.
expectedTests: Generator snapshot tests whose expected output files now include ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on every generated type.
A test that compiles generated code and checks by reflection that each generated type has ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute.

expectedBehaviours: The attribute shows up in generated code with default generator settings, with no MSBuild property, analyzer option or attribute argument needed.
A project with no MessagePack-specific configuration gets the attribute on its generated code.
expectedTests: A snapshot test that runs with default options and expects the attribute in the output.

expectedBehaviours: Generated object formatters carry the attribute.
Generated enum formatters carry the attribute.
Generated resolver types, including nested or helper types the resolver emits, carry the attribute.
Formatters for unions, custom or generic formatters, and any other generated kind carry the attribute too.
expectedTests: Snapshot tests that cover an object formatter, an enum formatter and a resolver, each showing the attribute.
A snapshot test for a union or generic type that shows the attribute on its generated formatter.

expectedBehaviours: Generated code is correct and compiles whether or not a GeneratedCode attribute is present.
If a GeneratedCode attribute is added, it is used consistently and does not cause duplicate-attribute compile errors.

Projects that target older frameworks where ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is missing or cannot be applied to all targets still build, with no CS0246 'type not found' error and no CS0592 'attribute not valid on this declaration type' error.
Generated code refers to the attribute in a way that resolves on every target framework the package supports, for example netstandard2.0, net472 and current .NET.
No new compiler warnings or errors appear in multi-targeted consumer projects.
expectedTests: Compile generated code against netstandard2.0 or another older reference set and assert that it builds with no errors.
Run the generator test suite across the supported target frameworks and confirm the generated code compiles.

expectedBehaviours: Diffs of the generated snapshot files show only the added attribute lines and nothing else.
Serialization and deserialization behave exactly as before, and existing round-trip tests pass unchanged.
No existing analyzer diagnostics change, and no new diagnostics appear because of the attribute.
expectedTests: The existing generator snapshot tests pass after their expected files are updated only to add the attribute.
The existing serialization round-trip tests that use generated formatters pass unchanged.

story.what: Every T4 template the MessagePack source generator uses to emit types now writes [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] inside an #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK guard. The templates covered are the object formatter, string-key formatter, enum, union, resolver and composite resolver; for the resolvers the attribute also goes on the nested FormatterCache<T> and GetFormatterHelper classes. Each .tt template and its checked-in .cs output were edited the same way. TransformUtilities now ends the opening brace of a nesting type that has constraints with a line break, so the #if that follows starts on its own line. A new test class runs the generator and checks that every generated file has the attribute and that every occurrence sits inside the guard. The snapshot files and the README were updated to match.
story.why: MP-2297 asks for all generated MessagePack code to be left out of code coverage reports through ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, with no setting needed, for formatters, enum formatters and resolvers, and without breaking builds on targets the author considers unable to use the attribute.

Writes the guarded attribute on the composite resolver class and its FormatterCache<T>.
Writes a line break after the opening brace of a nesting type that has type constraints.
New tests that run the generator and check that the attribute is present and guarded in every generated file.

findings.title: Guard drops coverage attribute on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework
findings.detail: Every template wraps the attribute in #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK. The comment in the test and the README say this is because the attribute is missing on those targets, but that is not true. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in .NET Framework 4.0 and later and in netstandard2.0, and classes are a valid target there. Only the Assembly target was added later, and the generator never uses it. So consumers that build for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework never get the attribute, and their generated formatters and resolvers still show up in coverage reports. That breaks F1 ('All generated code is decorated') and F2 for a large group of users: libraries targeting netstandard2.0, Unity projects and net4x apps. The guard buys nothing for N1, because the attribute would compile on those targets without it. The README states the same wrong reason in h1. The new test ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable makes the guard a required pattern, so it would fail if the guard were removed. The fix is to emit the attribute without a guard and update the snapshots, the README and the test.
